patch.value: GH-969: brief item reads can exceed standard output because omission receipts bill empty fields

The brief get/show projection can emit more bytes than standard because full restore hints are added for empty or default-valued fields that were cheaper to render. Preserve omission honesty while making depth cost monotone and agent-predictable.

Brief output never exceeds standard output for the same item and format; Empty or default-valued omissions do not incur a larger receipt than the value they replace; Property and integration tests cover monotone brief standard deep and full projection costs without hiding material omissions
Create a small item with comments and notes, then compare byte counts for show --depth brief, standard, deep, and full.
Projection depth is monotone in emitted cost while every material omission remains discoverable.
Brief measured 1400 bytes versus 1313 bytes for standard because restore hints cost more than empty body and unclaimed state.
Agents cannot trust the low-context depth control and spend more context while requesting less.
